title: SAMPLE — Statute, rule, and case excerpt
matter_name: SAMPLE — Suppression vehicle and SCA standard
warning_banner: SAMPLE excerpt. Not a real filing. Not legal advice. This pack shows citation verification across cases, a U.S. Code section, and a criminal rule — not a research memo and not a recommendation to file.
excerpt:
SAMPLE — NOT A REAL FILING
United States District Court, [Sample Jurisdiction]

The suppression motion is the proper vehicle for this objection. Fed. R. Crim. P. 12(b)(3)(C). The Stored Communications Act permits a court order for certain records on a standard below probable cause. 18 U.S.C. § 2703(d). That statutory standard does not displace the warrant requirement for historical cell-site location information. Carpenter v. United States, 585 U.S. 946 (2018). See also U.S. Const. amend. IV.

The court of appeals decision that preceded the Supreme Court opinion is United States v. Carpenter, 819 F.3d 880 (6th Cir. 2016). Cite it for procedural history, not as the current Fourth Amendment rule.
